statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6 (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress 53 (elevated) after Washington rejected Iran's seven-day Strait of Hormuz roadmap and with Friday's close leaving the ten-year Treasury yield at a post-crisis 5.18% and October rate-hike odds near 66%.
recommendation: Tail stays in the 6-9 band and far below the 25 blocking threshold in every assessed hour, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON across the whole window. No danger window is published: a market that does not trade cannot supply the observed price-path evidence a narrow evidence-based window requires, and the CME reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday falls four hours beyond the end of this forecast. Elevated Stress describes a difficult environment that may still mean-revert, and is reported separately from the Tail-derived state.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6 while rejected Hormuz diplomacy and 66% October hike odds lift Stress to 53
body: Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, four hours after this forecast window closes, so every assessed hour is structurally incapable of containing an observed price path. Friday's completed session argues against pathological structure rather than for it: NDX closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.53% below its 52-week high of 30,770.63, with VIX down 5.11% to 14.87 and the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite all notching weekly gains despite the bond sell-off. That is a two-way auction closing away from both extremes, so Tail is held at 6. Stress is a different question and edges up to 53. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed on day 210 after President Trump rejected Tehran's seven-day reopening roadmap on Saturday and President Pezeshkian said Iran has no trust in the American side, which withdraws the specific catalyst behind the roughly 8% weekly fall in U.S. crude to 92.41 and leaves Brent near 104.32. The rate path compounds that: the ten-year reached 5.18% on Friday, a post-crisis high, with the official H.15 series showing 4.87% at two years and 5.47% at thirty years through 24 September, and markets ended the week pricing roughly a 66% probability of an October Fed hike and 52% for December while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh attributed the long-end move to economic strength. A Reuters analysis of roughly $4.3 trillion of U.S. corporate bond maturities from 2027 frames the refinancing cost of that level. Shared latest-session context was mildly constructive beneath the surface, with megacaps 6 of 8 higher and semiconductors 6 of 7 higher, but it is delayed and non-real-time and cannot establish current structure; its futures and calendar sections were unavailable in this collection. Confidence of 80 reflects verified index, futures, volatility, yield and energy levels together with a verified seven-day calendar, discounted for the structurally absent live tape and for those two missing shared-context sections.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, so none is unavailable. The window opens in the final hours of Friday's U.S. cash session, where Tail ran 18-19 with EA_ON mapped throughout and Stress held in the mid-50s under a mixed mode. After Friday's 21:00Z futures settlement Tail decayed from 12 to 8 and Stress eased from 50 into the mid-40s as the session's directional question closed out and the mode moved to normal. Through Saturday the halt kept Tail flat at 7-8 while Stress rebuilt from 44 to 52 as the Hormuz diplomacy deteriorated, and Confidence drifted from the high 80s to 80-83 as the last tradable tape aged. No hour in the window was mapped above green, and no historical opinion has been restated with later information.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forecast hours falls inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00Z on Sunday, four hours past the end of this window, so no hour can contain observed price-path structure. Tail is held in a 6-9 band throughout and stays far below the 25 blocking threshold, mapping EA_ON and green in every slot. The step from 6 to 7 at the start of Sunday and to 8 and then 9 through Sunday afternoon is accumulated unpriced gap risk ahead of a single reopening auction, not observed one-way structure. Stress traces the weekend news-flow windows, easing to 49 in the thin overnight hours and building to 55 late on Sunday on the unresolved strait closure, Brent near 104 and a rate path now pricing an October hike. Confidence decays from 80 to 73 purely because the newest observable tape ages past 48 hours with no replacement possible before the reopen. The conditional branch that would matter is the shape of that reopen: an orderly two-way auction with genuine retracement would validate the low Tail carried here, while immediate one-way extension holding near an extreme would be the first real amplifier.
